summary: Steel fire tower with a New Hampshire wooden cab on Mount Belknap in Belknap County; built 1914-15, raised 1979, refurbished 2023, NHLR-registered 2002, in active service.

corrections.why: NHLR gives a 34 ft steel tower plus a 10 ft addition in 1979, about 44 ft or 13.4 m. The record's 121.9 m is about 400 ft, which no source gives.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Historic Structures says the steel tower was constructed in 1914-1915 and NHLR says 1915. Trailspotting says a fire tower has been on the mountain since 1913. Story uses 1914-1915 and notes the 1913 claim.

NHLR lists the NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development as administrator, with NH Division of Forests and Lands as cooperator. The 2023 newsletter and Historic Structures refer to the Division of Forests & Lands. The record keeps the NHLR listing; a newer state agency name may apply and is not verified.

notes_for_editor: Brief's height_m 121.9 (about 400 ft) is not supported; NHLR's 34 ft tower plus 1979 10 ft addition gives 13.4 m, and that is proposed as the correction. Build date: 1914-15 (Historic Structures), 1915 (NHLR), 1913 (Trailspotting), left as a stated conflict. Agency: NHLR names the NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development; a search snippet pointed to a dncr.nh.gov news release, which returned 403 when fetched, so the newer agency name is unverified and not cited. Final 2023 costs and the actual 2024 reopening are not confirmed beyond the newsletter's expectation and Trailspotting's 2025 'refurbished in 2023' statement. Staffing: NHLR's 2016 visit report says 'Sometimes' staffed, during fire season; no current staffing source found. No specific fires were named in sources read. Left out on purpose: a 1952 death at the lookout cabin in the Forest Lookouts item and a 1957 newspaper mention of a named lookout, since they concern private individuals and are not needed for the tower's history. The Historic Structures page is a third-party history site; its dates are cited as its own claims. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with public trail access and seasonal road-gate hours from Trailspotting; climbing the cab is not stated in any source. Budget note: the Historic Structures page was grepped several times from cache; it counts as one page.
